investigators.summary: The swapped-pinout hypothesis is refuted, on four independent grounds that each rule it out alone. Suppose a part with pin 1 REF, pin 2 K, pin 3 A (TL432 DBZ, or the Changjiang CJ431 / onsemi SN / Diodes AZ431 style SOT-23) sat on the TI TL431 DBZ footprint. Its REF pin would then be fed from V-MOT through R-GS 3.3k and R-G 220. That pulls VG down onto the 12 V zener clamp, Vgs = -11.4 to -12.7 V, and the BSP170P turns hard on from V-MOT ~4-6 V upward. The 47 ohm dump would then conduct continuously: 0.34 A and 5.4 W at 15.93 V. The REF pin would carry 4-13 mA, already at or over the 10 mA absolute maximum. The tap (now the cathode) would be clamped flat near the Darlington knee instead of tracking V-MOT. None of this matches the logs. Idle bus load is ~0-0.03 A. The post-regen-peak fall is linear at 11.1-12.2 V/s (reading units), which bounds the V-MOT node's net load to 7-20 mA, against the 0.38-0.43 A the dump would draw. The tap swings 1.50 -> 2.06 V during regen bursts, and the 6.12 V collapse sample reads 0.685 V, against a predicted flat clamp of ~0.9-1.9 V (reading >= ~8-17 V). The other plausible pin permutations either forward-bias the anode-cathode substrate diode or REF into VG (dump on again), or ground REF and float the anode on the tap (a source, not a 31 uA sink); none produces the signature. In the as-designed orientation a HEALTHY TL431 cannot sink 31 uA either. The TL431BI REF current is 2 typ / 4 max uA, plus at most 2.5 uA deviation over temperature, i.e. <= ~6.5 uA, giving a ratio >= 0.968. TI Fig 6-2 shows REF current FALLING as the part warms, so a healthy part would make the ratio rise with warm-up; the logs show it falling. The leak is therefore an abnormal path that grows as the board warms: a damaged TL431 REF input (base-emitter or base-collector junction, or lost current gain), a leaking Teensy pin-39 pad, or board contamination. The DMM node check in doc section 6 remains the decisive next step, and a 10 s check of Vgs on Q-SNT or the temperature of R-SHUNT is enough to close the swapped-pinout question on the bench.

hypotheses.name: Swapped TL431 pinout (TL432-style: pin1 REF, pin2 K, pin3 A) fitted on the TI TL431 DBZ footprint
hypotheses.predictions: Model: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-DC-Balancer-Board-Teensy/2dd4079b-96a3-52c6-9594-2aa3f1f11188/scratchpad/wf/tl431-orientation/model.py. Assumptions: the TL431 Detailed Schematic (Fig 8-2, datasheet p.21) treated as REF->anode through 2 junctions + 3.28k, REF->cathode through the input NPN's B-C diode, and a cathode Darlington knee Vk swept 0.8-1.8 V. Footprint pin 1 = REF sits behind R-G 220 on the VG side; footprint pin 2 = cathode = RGN-V tap; pin 3 = GND. Results: (a) DC point at 15.93 V. REF pin at 1.9-2.0 V. REF current 3.8-13.1 mA (zener clamps VG at V-MOT - Vz, Vz 11.4-12.7 V), at or above the 10 mA abs max. Vgs = -11.4 to -12.7 V, so Q-SNT is fully enhanced. Dump current = V-MOT/(47+0.3) = 0.339 A, 5.4 W in R-SHUNT. Tap = 0.90-1.91 V depending on Vk, roughly flat. (b) Tap against V-MOT (Vk 1.1 V): 0.35 V at 1 V, 1.01 V at 3 V, 1.10 V at 6.1 V (reading 9.76, observed 6.08), 1.15 V at 12.2 V, 1.21 V at 15.93 V, 1.27 V at 20.3 V, 1.32 V at 30 V. Reading 9-12 V for any V-MOT >= 3 V. It cannot reach 2.05 V at a regen peak: that needs ~0.5 V above the knee, i.e. >100 mA injected, against <=0.25 mA available through R1. The tap/ideal ratio falls from 3.0 to 0.39 across the range instead of staying at 0.85. (c) Temperature: a junction-knee clamp falls ~-2 to -4 mV/C, the same direction as the warm-up drift, but this is moot. (d) Trip: the dump turns on from V-MOT = 3.96 / 4.96 / 6.05 V for BSP170P Vgs(th) = -2.1 / -3 / -4 V and never turns off. The 'chopper' is permanently on, never a 22.13 V trip, and the REF current passes 10 mA abs max above ~16 V.
hypotheses.evidence: AGAINST, four independent grounds. (1) Standing load. The model predicts 0.339 A on the bus at 15.93 V. The doc measures idle I_fc+I_batt ~0.008-0.03 A (docs/vrgn_measurement_error_2026-11-05.md section 2). My YP0166 window shows I_fc+I_batt = 0.000-0.016 A at 119.2-120.0 s (logs/YP0166/YP0166.csv). (2) Node discharge rate. The post-peak falls of all 14 regen peaks above a 16.5 V reading (ML0151, ML0157, ML0165, ML0195, ...) are linear at 11.1-12.2 V/s reading (one outlier at 74.5 V/s). That is ~14 V/s true, so the node net load is 6.7-19.6 mA for C = 480 uF to 1.4 mF (doc section 5 bounds). A conducting dump gives 0.38-0.43 A at 18-20 V and an exponential decay with tau = 47*C = 23-66 ms. Measured with fall.py in the scratch dir. (3) Proportionality. The tap swings 1.50 -> 2.06 V in bursts (YP0166 reading 13.33 -> 17.55). The collapse sample WP0097 reads 6.08 at bus 6.12 (tap 0.685 V, needing only 0.5 uA of leak). The swapped model gives a near-constant ~1.1-1.5 V. (4) The REF current would sit at 4-13 mA, against II(ref) abs max 10 mA (TL431_TI.pdf section 6.1, text line 203). A swapped part would have been overstressed every time the bus was up since 2026-08-12, yet the ratio has stayed stable for 3 months. Also: R-SHUNT at 5.4 W would be hot to the touch. Supply chain: the BOM orders the genuine TI TL431BIDBZR from Digikey (BOM CSV line 35), and the assembly BOM lists an Ultra Librarian TL431BIDBZR DBZ0003A_N footprint (Scale Car Board BOM.txt line 49; PnP_Scale Car Board_front.txt line 115, U-SNT rotation 270). Pad-to-net mapping on the copper was not checked from the gerbers.

hypotheses.name: As-designed orientation, HEALTHY TL431BI: REF input current alone draws the 31 uA
hypotheses.predictions: Tap drop = Iref x (R1||R2 = 8.873 k). Iref 2 uA gives ratio 0.990, 4 uA gives 0.980, 6.5 uA (max + full II(dev) 2.5) gives 0.968. 0.85 needs Iref ~31.5 uA. Below Vref (REF 1.52 V < 2.495 V) the input NPN runs at lower emitter current, so Iref should be at or below the spec value, not above it. Temperature: TI Fig 6-2 has Iref falling from ~2.5 uA at -50 C to ~1.5 uA at 125 C, so warm-up should RAISE the ratio slightly.
hypotheses.evidence: TL431_TI.pdf section 6.12 (TL431BI), text lines ~543-575: Iref 2 typ / 4 max uA at IKA 10 mA, R1 10k; II(dev) 0.8 typ / 2.5 max uA; Ioff 0.1/0.5 uA. The required leak is 29.5-33.5 uA across ratios 0.854-0.834 at 15.9 V (model.py), 4.8x the conservative worst case. Fig 6-2 (p.15) has a negative TC, against the measured ratio falling with uptime (corr -0.80..-0.97, doc section 3).

hypotheses.name: As-designed orientation, ABNORMAL junction leak on the RGN-V node (damaged TL431 REF input, e.g. B-E/B-C leakage or gain loss from reverse-EB/ESD stress; or the Teensy pin-39 pad)
hypotheses.predictions: ~30-33 uA sink at a 1.5 V node that grows with temperature (as junction leakage does). Sub-uA at a 0.69 V node would also be consistent with the WP0097 single sample (0.5 uA needed), i.e. strongly voltage-nonlinear, BUT that sample is unreliable (V-MOT may sit above V_bus). Q-SNT stays off (VG = V-MOT minus ~Ioff x 3.3k, i.e. mV), and the dump never conducts. Consistent with the 7-20 mA node-load bound and the zero idle load.
hypotheses.evidence: Required leak 30.9 uA at 15.93 V, 9.5 uA at 12.19 V (TP0115), 0.5 uA at 6.12 V (WP0097) (model.py; the collapse samples are unreliable). The temperature sign matches a junction leak and is opposite to a healthy TL431's Iref TC (Fig 6-2). This test cannot tell the TL431 apart from the Teensy pad (the V_chg channel on an identical divider reads 0.994, which argues against an ADC-wide fault but not against a single damaged pad). This is the residual explanation once orientation and a healthy part are excluded. Not proven.

hypotheses.name: Other pin permutations (anode on VG or on the tap, REF grounded)
hypotheses.predictions: (A on VG, REF on tap, K on GND): the anode-cathode substrate diode is forward biased (Fig 6-3: -100 mA at ~-1.9 V), VG is pulled low, and the dump turns on. (REF on VG, A on tap, K on GND): the substrate diode clamps the tap to ~0.7 V, REF pulls VG down, and the dump turns on. (K on VG, A on tap, REF on GND): REF sits below the anode, the part is off, and the floating anode/substrate SOURCES ~Ioff into the tap (reads high, not a 31 uA sink); the chopper could never trip.
hypotheses.evidence: Qualitative, from TI Fig 8-1/8-2 (p.21) and Fig 6-3/6-4 (p.15). The first two again imply a continuous 0.34 A dump (refuted by the same load and decay data). The third gives the wrong sign of error. No common SOT-23 TL431 variant found online uses these orders (sources found disagree only between K-REF-A and REF-K-A).

investigators.summary: The four handoff dips in the logs give a measured I-V curve for the node leak, and a damaged TL431 input stage (correct orientation) fits it well. In each dip the bus dropped from 15.9 V to about 12.2 V for 5-8 ms while MOT_PWR was closed and the motor was drawing current, so V-MOT followed V_bus. In all four events the leak behaves like a threshold plus a resistor: I = (V_node - Von)/R with Von 1.19-1.25 V and R 9.2-9.3 k, rms 1 uA. A resistor to GND fits 7x worse and a constant current 8x worse. A reverse-junction leak is also ruled out, because the current grows 3.3x over 0.21 V. A healthy TL431 draws only about 0.5-1 uA at 1.52 V (scaled from SLVS543S Table 6.12 and Fig 6-2), and its REF current falls as it warms, the opposite of what the logs show. The knee is about two Vbe and R is the same order as the TL431's internal REF path (input transistor Vbe + diode Vbe + 3.28k + 2.4k, Fig 8-2). So the best physical match is an input transistor whose current gain has collapsed (REF current roughly equal to its emitter current), with warm-up drift of -2 mV/degC at the node, which needs only a 1-2 degC rise within a session. In-circuit overstress of REF is very unlikely: the 78.7k divider limits REF current to 0.5 mA even at 40 V, against a 10 mA abs max, and no bench event shows V-MOT negative or above 37 V. ESD, handling, assembly or a wrong/clone part are more likely, and the error was already there on 2026-08-12. The I-V shape alone does not single out the TL431 over a Teensy-pad path with a similar knee; a freeze-spray test or a lifted REF pin would settle it. Safety consequence if the leak is on the node: extrapolating this I-V puts the effective chopper trip at about 33 V of V-MOT and the recorded regen peaks at about 25 V true (not 21.5 V), above the RT1987's 32 V operating limit.

hypotheses.name: Healthy TL431 REF bias current (in spec)
hypotheses.predictions: REF current = Q1 base current, about Ie/beta. Scaled from Iref 2 uA typ / 4 uA max at REF = 2.495 V with a 2-Vbe (~1.2 V) knee, it is about 0.49-0.99 uA at 1.52 V, giving 4-9 mV of node error (0.3-0.6 % of the ratio). It falls as the part warms (Fig 6-2: about 2.5 uA at -55 C down to 1.45 uA at 125 C).
hypotheses.evidence: TL431BI Iref 2 typ / 4 max uA and II(dev) 0.8 typ / 2.5 max uA (references/Datasheets/TL431_TI.pdf, SLVS543S Table 6.12, p.13); Fig 6-2 p.15 shows Iref falling with temperature. Observed: 29.5-33.6 uA (30-60x too large), and the leak rises with warm-up (wrong sign).

hypotheses.name: Damaged TL431: resistive REF-anode leak (ESD-melted filament, conductive contamination, ~50-60 k)
hypotheses.predictions: Leak proportional to node voltage, so V_rgn/V_bus is constant at every voltage. Metal or doped-silicon filaments have a positive resistance TC, so the leak would fall when warm.
hypotheses.evidence: Measured dip I-V (logs TP0115/TP0178/TP0201/TP0209; scratch dips.csv, fitmodels.py): a through-origin resistor fits with rms 6.7-7.0 uA against 1.0-1.1 uA for threshold-linear. The ratio rises from 0.835 at 15.9 V to 0.939 at 12.15 V on the same event. On the rising branch the ideal diode forces V-MOT <= V_bus, so the true ratio there is >= 0.91 at about 13 V. The warm-up sign is also wrong (leak grows when warm).

hypotheses.name: Damaged TL431: reverse-biased junction leakage (REF-substrate / reverse E-B damage; current-source-like, doubles per ~8-10 C)
hypotheses.predictions: Current nearly independent of the 1.3-1.5 V reverse bias. In-session node drift = -8.87k x dI, with dI about 7 %/C x 31 uA, which gives about 19 mV/C at the node.
hypotheses.evidence: The measured leak goes from 9.4 to 33 uA (3.5x) over node 1.286 to 1.497 V (TP0178 event), which is not current-source behaviour; a constant-current fit has rms 8 uA. The observed in-session node shift of 2.3-4.6 mV (ratio drop 0.15-0.3 %, docs/vrgn_measurement_error_2026-11-05.md section 3) would mean only a 0.12-0.24 C warm-up under this model, which is implausibly small next to the 1.8 % session-to-session spread.

hypotheses.name: Damaged TL431 input stage, correct orientation: Q1 (REF emitter follower) has lost its gain (open collector or beta << 1), so REF current is about the chain current through Vbe(Q1) + Vbe(diode-connected Q) + 3.28k + 2.4k (||7.2k branch)
hypotheses.predictions: I_ref is about (V_REF - 2Vbe)/R_chain: knee about 1.1-1.3 V, R a few k to about 10 k. Below the knee the leak is about 0, so the ratio tends to 1.00 at V-MOT <= 10 V. Node TC about -2 mV/C (Von TC about -4.2 mV/C x Rth/(R+Rth) = 0.494). The bandgap is untouched, so the chopper still trips at REF = 2.495 V, which then needs V-MOT of about 33 V. No extra cathode current, so the dump stays off.
hypotheses.evidence: FOR: the measured I-V knee Von is 1.193 / 1.196 / 1.226 / 1.245 V and R is 9.23-9.34 k, nearly constant across 13-25 Aug sessions (fitmodels.py). A diode+R fit needs a single-diode Is of about 1e-26 A, which is the signature of two stacked junctions. ML0227 (fw v37, J session, V_chg = V-MOT minus a drop) brackets the leak at node 1.485 V between 23.2 and 28.4 uA; the model predicts 25.5 uA. The collapse samples fit: WP0097 6.12 V reads 0.993 (model 1.00); TP0115 12.19 V reads 0.938 (model 0.94). The warm-up sign is right, and the in-session ratio drop of 0.15-0.3 % needs only a 1.1-2.2 C die rise. The topology is from Fig 8-2 (p.21): REF goes to the Q1 base, the Q1 emitter goes to 3.28k, then to 2.4k plus a diode-connected Q and to 7.2k. AGAINST / UNKNOWN: measured R is about 1.6x the nominal 3.28k+2.4k = 5.68k (diffused-resistor tolerance or residual beta could explain it, but it is unverified). The 57 mV Von shift between the 0.835 era (mid-Aug) and the 0.850 era (late Aug onward) needs about 14 C, or slow annealing of the damage. Only four dip events exist, all on 13-25 Aug. No in-circuit overstress path found (see new_facts). A Teensy-pad or other leak with a similar ~1.2 V knee is not excluded by the I-V alone.

hypotheses.name: TL431 cathode-REF (Q1 collector-base) breakdown or leak from VKA transients
hypotheses.predictions: Current flows from the cathode (about V-MOT through 3.3k + 220 ohm) into REF, so REF reads HIGH (ratio > 1).
hypotheses.evidence: Wrong sign: the observed reading is low. VKA has never been near the 37 V abs max in the logs (regen peaks 21.5 V true in case B, about 25 V in case A).

hypotheses.name: Leak into the TL431 error-amp/driver node (REF to the diode-connected device in Fig 8-2, then into the Darlington driver)
hypotheses.predictions: Leak current would also feed the Darlington base, so the cathode would sink (beta^2 gain) and pull VG down. The knee would sit near the driver-node level (about 0-0.2 V when off), not 1.2 V.
hypotheses.evidence: The measured knee at 1.2 V does not match. Cathode sink below about 0.64 mA (BSP170P VGS(th) min -2.1 V at -250 uA / 3.3k R-GS; BSP170P_Infineon.pdf p.95 of the text extract) would not be seen in the bus current, so this path cannot be fully excluded remotely.

hypotheses.name: Wrong part fitted (TL432 pinout on the TL431 footprint)
hypotheses.predictions: REF lands on VG and the cathode on the tap. The REF overdrive makes the part sink hard, the zener clamps VGS at -12 V, and the dump conducts about 0.34 A continuously; the tap would not track V-MOT smoothly.
hypotheses.evidence: Idle bus load is 0.008-0.03 A, and the dip data show the node tracking V_bus smoothly on both branches. TL432 DBZ is pin1 REF / pin2 CATHODE (SLVS543S pinout).

TL431 REF input topology (references/Datasheets/TL431_TI.pdf Fig 8-2, p.21): REF drives the base of NPN Q1 (collector to CATHODE). The Q1 emitter goes through 3.28 kOhm to a node, then 2.4 kOhm to a diode-connected NPN to ANODE, and in parallel 7.2 kOhm to the bandgap transistor (800 ohm emitter). A diode-connected device also ties REF to the error-amp/driver node. Section 8.3: 'the reference pin is driven into an npn, which needs base current'.

Section 10.6: ESD damage 'can range from subtle performance degradation to complete device failure'.

In-circuit REF overstress is current-limited: through R1-SNT 78.7k, REF current is at most 40/78.7k = 0.5 mA even at the RT1987's 40 V abs max (20x below the 10 mA abs max). investigators.summary: An intact Teensy 4.1 pin-39 pad or ADC path cannot account for the roughly 31 uA load. Every mechanism that a correctly working i.MX RT1062 or the Teensy core software could produce is ruled out, either by the numbers or because it would hit pin 38 equally. Pins 38 and 39 are adjacent channels (1 and 2) on the same ADC2 instance, on the same pad type (GPIO_AD_B1_12 and _13). They share one global ADC configuration, and the firmware never configures either pad. The keeper (105-175 kOhm, at most 14.5 uA at 1.52 V), the only pull to ground (the 100k pull-down, at most about 22 uA) and the specified input leakage (1 uA max) each fall short of the roughly 49 kOhm equivalent load needed. Analogread also turns the keeper off. The node goes to 2.05 V for about 240 ms in every regen burst and returns to the same ratio, so no latching keeper is involved. ADC sampling settles in 87 time constants. What remains is a DAMAGED pin-39 pad (an ESD-structure leak to GND at least 30 times the datasheet limit). It fits all the data and has a plausible exposure route: V-MOT sits behind the RT1987 ideal diode and holds charge for about 110 s, so pin 39 can be driven while the Teensy's 3.3 V is off, which NXP says must not happen. But nothing in the logs separates it from a TL431 REF leak, because both load the same node. The Teensy plugs into receptacles J1/J2, so a cheap lab test settles it in minutes. One caution against any junction-leak explanation (pad or TL431): the warm-up drift corresponds to only about a 2 % rise in leak current per session.

hypotheses.name: i.MX pad keeper (PKE=1, PUE=0 reset default) loading pin 39
hypotheses.predictions: To pull an 8.873 kOhm / 1.796 V Thevenin source down to 1.522 V needs about 49.3 kOhm to GND (31 uA). If the keeper were latched low, it would behave the same on pin 38 and would flip high once the node crossed the input threshold, after which the reading would sit HIGH (ratio about 1.1).
hypotheses.evidence: (1) Too weak. The keeper resistance R_Keeper is 105-175 kOhm (IMXRT1060CEC Rev 4, Table 22, p.38), so it can draw at most 8.7-14.5 uA at 1.52 V. (2) The core turns it off. teensy4/analog.c analogRead() clears PKE when PKE=1 and PUE=0 (PaulStoffregen/cores, added in commit c5e7163 on 2024-01-15). The firmware never calls pinMode on pin 38 or 39, so both pads stay at the reset default, which is keeper on every GPIO_AD_B1 pad (datasheet pin-list table). (3) Same pad type and same treatment on pin 38, which reads 0.994. (4) Data (my scan, scratch burst2.py): in YP0196, ML0151, ML0195, YP0198 and ML0157 the node goes above 1.70 V for 216-264 samples and peaks at 2.04-2.05 V. The ratio 1-5 s later matches the pre-burst ratio to within 0.0007. There is no latch and no step larger than 0.47 V per sample.

hypotheses.name: Pad pull resistor enabled on pin 39
hypotheses.predictions: The only pull to GND is the 100k pull-down, and it would have to be configured on pin 39 only.
hypotheses.evidence: Pull-down current is at most 48 uA at Vin = NVCC (Table 22, p.38), which scales to at most about 22 uA at 1.52 V. That is short of 31 uA, and nothing enables a pull on pin 39: grep shows no pinMode, IOMUXC or portControlRegister use for 38/39 in teensy_controller.ino, and analog.c lines 111-119 leave existing pulls untouched.

hypotheses.name: ADC source impedance / sampling-time error (8.87 kOhm too high for the default config)
hypotheses.predictions: A charge-sharing error would depend on the previous channel and on sample time, and would be identical on pin 38, which has the same 8.87 kOhm source.
hypotheses.evidence: Core config (analog.c lines 153, 230, 243, 259, 267): async ADACK, ADIV=1, ADHSC=1, ADLSMP=1, ADSTS=3. That gives fADACK 20 MHz (Table 55, p.66), so fADCK = 10 MHz, and 24 sample cycles = 2.4 us. RADIN is at most 7 kOhm and CADIN at most 2 pF (Table 54, p.64-65), so tau = 27.7 ns and the sample lasts about 87 tau, fully settled. The 1 kOhm RAS limit applies only to 150 ns sampling at 40 MHz. Average switched-capacitor current is about 0.1 uA. Carry-over is already ruled out by ML0227 (0.84739 with V_chg at 0 V and at 15.8 V).

hypotheses.name: ADC channel / instance defect (case B: node correct, conversion wrong)
hypotheses.predictions: A gain or offset error specific to ADC2 channel 2 of about 15 %, or 339 counts. A DMM would read 1.80 V on the node.
hypotheses.evidence: Pins 38 and 39 both use ADC2 only (analog.c lines 81-82), with the same conversion settings and calibration. Datasheet TUE is at most 4.28 LSB, offset at most 0.07 %FSV and gain at most 0.03 %FSV (Table 55, p.67), orders of magnitude below 339 counts. A reading error without a real node load would need a channel-specific mux defect, and that does not fit a temperature-drifting leak. A pad leak would show up as case A, not case B.

hypotheses.name: Alternate peripheral function driving or loading pin 39 (SPI1 MISO1, SAI)
hypotheses.predictions: Pin 39 would only be loaded if LPSPI3 or another peripheral muxed the pad.
hypotheses.evidence: In the Teensy 4.1 SPI library, pin 39 is an alternate MISO for SPI1 (LPSPI3) and pin 38 an alternate CS (PaulStoffregen/SPI SPI.cpp lines 1568 and 1580). The firmware only uses SPI (LPSPI4) on pins 11/12/13 (teensy_controller.ino:16265-16268), Serial1 on pins 0/1 and USB Serial. grep finds no SPI1, setCS, I2S or SAI.

hypotheses.name: Damaged pin-39 pad (ESD clamp / input structure leaking to GND)
hypotheses.predictions: This is case A: a DMM reads about 1.52 V on the node, and the node recovers to about 1.80 V with the Teensy unplugged from J1/J2. On an unpowered Teensy, pin 39 measures lower to GND than pin 38 in ohms or diode mode. If the leak is junction-like it follows Teensy die temperature.
hypotheses.evidence: For: an intact pad leaks at most 1 uA (Table 22, p.38), so 31 uA needs damage at least 30 times the limit. Pin 38's 0.994 ratio puts at most about 1.2 uA on its node, within spec, so a pin-specific defect is exactly what pin 38 vs 39 requires. Exposure route (inferred): V-MOT is isolated by the RT1987 ideal diode and holds charge with a tau of 105-122 s (ML0215-ML0217). The Teensy is board-powered from an LM1084 off VBT (PLAN.md:1771) and browned out on 2026-07-08 with MOT_PWR closed onto the VESC (docs/boost-bringup-debug.md:188). Pin 39 can therefore sit at 1.8-2 V with NVCC off, back-injecting about 135-155 uA. That violates absolute-max Vin (OVDD+0.3 V, Table 7, p.24) and section 4.2.1.3 (p.31), which warns of latch-up from reverse current. Against: the V_batt and V_fc nodes could also inject in some power sequences, so pin 39's exposure is not proven unique. The current, limited by 8.87 kOhm, is only about 0.15 mA. The warm-up drift is only a +1.8 % leak rise (32.8 -> 33.4 uA, ML0164 -> TP0180), weak for a junction leak; the same objection applies to a TL431 junction. The logs cannot separate this from a TL431 REF leak on the same node.

hypotheses.name: Teensy board swap exonerates or incriminates the pad
hypotheses.predictions: If the Teensy were swapped and the ratio did not change, the pad would be exonerated. If the ratio stepped at a swap, the pad would be implicated.
hypotheses.evidence: No record of a Teensy replacement in docs/*.md, WORK_QUEUE.md, docs/boost-bringup-debug.md or docs/claude-md-archive.md. Neither the BLG header nor the telemetry carries a Teensy serial number or MAC. The ratio has no step from 2026-08-12 onward.

new_facts: Teensy 4.1 pin 38 = A14 = GPIO_AD_B1_12 and pin 39 = A15 = GPIO_AD_B1_13 (cores teensy4/core_pins.h lines 1046-1047 and 1103-1104; pins_arduino.h lines 66-67). Both are ADC2-only, channels 1 and 2 (cores teensy4/analog.c lines 81-82), so the V_chg and V_rgn readings use the same converter.

analogRead() on Teensy 4.x clears the pad keeper (PKE) when PKE=1 and PUE=0, and leaves user pulls alone (analog.c lines 111-119). This was added in cores commit c5e7163 on 2024-01-15. The Teensyduino version used is not recorded in the repo.
The firmware calls neither pinMode nor any pad configuration on pin 38 or 39. Both pads stay at the i.MX reset default (keeper, per the IMXRT1060CEC pin-list table), so both get identical treatment.

Core ADC configuration: async ADACK, ADIV=1, ADHSC=1, 12-bit, ADLSMP=1, ADSTS=3 (analog.c lines 153, 230, 243, 259, 267), with 16-sample averaging set by the firmware (teensy_controller.ino:6682). Datasheet: fADACK = 20 MHz with ADHSC=1, 24 sample and 50 conversion cycles (IMXRT1060CEC Rev 4, Table 55, p.66). So sampling lasts 2.4 us at 10 MHz, and a 16-sample read takes about 80 us.

i.MX RT1060 GPIO and ADC limits: IIN -1..+1 uA; R_Keeper 105-175 kOhm; 100k pull-down current at most 48 uA at Vin = NVCC (Table 22, p.38). CADIN at most 2 pF and RADIN 5-7 kOhm with ADHSC=1 (Table 54, p.64-65). Absolute maximum Vin -0.5 to OVDD+0.3 V (Table 7, p.24). Section 4.2.1.3 (p.31): I/O must not be driven while NVCC is off. Source: https://www.pjrc.com/teensy/IMXRT1060CEC_rev4.pdf

Required load (computed): Thevenin source 8.873 kOhm at 1.796 V, so a 1.522 V reading means 30.9 uA drawn off, equivalent to 49.3 kOhm to GND. The keeper gives at most 14.5 uA and the 100k pull-down at most about 22 uA at 1.52 V, so no in-spec pad state can produce the error.

Measured (my scan): in every regen burst the pin-39 node goes above 1.70 V for 216-264 ms and peaks at 2.04-2.05 V. The ratio afterwards returns to the pre-burst value within 0.0007 (YP0196 0.8464 -> 0.8459; ML0151 0.8437 -> 0.8434; ML0195 0.8468 -> 0.8461; YP0198 0.8457 -> 0.8451; ML0157 0.8370 -> 0.8364). No hysteresis or latch is present. Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-DC-Balancer-Board-Teensy/2dd4079b-96a3-52c6-9594-2aa3f1f11188/scratchpad/wf/teensy-pad/burst2.py

Pin 39 is an alternate MISO for SPI1 (LPSPI3) and pin 38 an alternate CS1 on Teensy 4.1 (PaulStoffregen/SPI SPI.cpp lines 1568 and 1580). The firmware never starts SPI1 and uses LPSPI4 on pins 11/12/13 (teensy_controller.ino:16265-16268).
The Teensy plugs into board receptacles J1/J2 (BOM line 54, Amphenol 87606-324LF), so it can be removed for a node measurement without desoldering.

The within-session warm-up corresponds to only a +1.8 % leak change (32.8 -> 33.4 uA at 15.9 V, from the doc's ML0164 -> TP0180 ratios 0.8375 -> 0.8346). The week-scale shift from 0.835 to 0.85 is about -10 %. That is a weak temperature coefficient for a junction leak.

Inferred exposure route: the Teensy is board-powered (LM1084 off VBT, PLAN.md:1771) and browned out on 2026-07-08 with MOT_PWR closed onto the VESC (docs/boost-bringup-debug.md:188). investigators.summary: The leak is strongly voltage-dependent and is close to zero at low voltage. It is not a constant current and not a resistor. Four independent bus-dip events (TP0115, TP0178, TP0201, TP0209; 12.2-15.9 V; V-MOT pinned to V_bus because V_rgn starts rising on the same 1 ms sample as V_bus) all give the same leak curve: zero below a threshold of 1.19-1.25 V at the node, then linear at 105-107 uA per V (1/g = 9.3-9.5 kOhm). The threshold moves with session or warm-up; the slope does not. The fw v37 J ramp (ML0227: 11 A through MOT_PWR+REGEN, so V_chg <= V-MOT <= V_bus) reproduces that curve if V-MOT sits about 0.36 of the way from V_bus to V_chg, which is what RT1987 RON 20 mOhm predicts. Its 6.8 V collapse samples put the ratio at 0.93-1.10, so the leak is about 0 at node 0.72 V. The quasi-static small-signal gain dV_rgn/dV_bus near 16 V measures 0.52-0.65 on four logs. The model predicts 0.513; a resistive leak would give 0.85 and a constant current 1.0. If the curve stays linear above the measured range (an extrapolation), the 18.26 V regen peak reading means V-MOT was about 24.6-25.0 V, and the chopper would trip near 33 V rather than 22.1 V. This holds only in case A (the leak is a real load on the node), which the 2026-11-05 doc's step-1 DMM check decides. Data cannot separate a threshold-plus-resistor element from a soft junction plus about 7.5-8.7 kOhm. Both fit, and both rule out exponential, constant-current and resistive leak models.

hypotheses.name: Threshold-linear / junction + series-R leak on the RGN-V node (onset ~1.2 V node, ~9.4 kOhm incremental)
hypotheses.predictions: I_leak = 0 for Vn < Vth; I_leak ~= g (Vn - Vth) above, g ~107 uA/V, Vth 1.19-1.25 V (lower when warm). Ratio V_rgn/V-MOT = 1.00 for V-MOT < ~10.6-11 V. Small-signal reading gain near 16 V = 8.87*(1/R1)/(1/R1+1/R2+g) = 0.513 V/V. Leak at node 2.495 V ~136 uA -> chopper trips at V-MOT ~32.9 V. 18.26 V peak reading (node 2.059 V) -> V-MOT ~24.6-25.0 V.
hypotheses.evidence: TP dips (dip_pts.csv, rising/falling branches averaged to cancel ADC skew): linear fit rms 0.15-0.26 uA; exponential 0.82-0.94; power law 0.68-0.81; square law 0.30-0.36; resistive-through-0 5.5; constant 6.4. Local slopes stay at 92-130 uA/V over 8-31 uA. g is the same in all four (105.5-107.4 uA/V). Vth is 1.197/1.192 V in the TP0115/0178 session (ratio 0.836) and 1.226/1.247 V in TP0201/0209 (ratio 0.845-0.850). That 50 mV shift reproduces the session ratio drift via dVn/dVth = 0.487. J ramp (ML0227 t 23.69-24.72 s) matches g = 107 at x = 0.36; at x = 0.5 it matches TP0209 to 0.1 uA at node 1.464 V. J collapse (24.7281/24.7292 s) leak bounds -7.5..+6.2 uA at node 0.716-0.723 V; the model predicts 0. Block-mean slopes dV_rgn/dV_bus: ML0203 0.521, TP0086 0.525, ML0169 0.571, ML0226 0.654 (corr 0.99-1.00). The step to 1.0 gain below Vth is not directly observed in quasi-static data; only bounded collapse and teardown points cover that range.

hypotheses.name: Soft junction (n~1-1.5) + ~7.4-8.7 kOhm series resistance (variant of the above)
hypotheses.predictions: Slight upward curvature of dI/dV at low current; same extrapolation as the linear model at higher current (series R dominates).
hypotheses.evidence: Fit V = a + nVt ln I + Rs I to the TP dips: nVt 13-38 mV, Rs 7.4-8.7 kOhm, node-voltage rms 1.0-1.2 mV vs 1.4-2.4 mV for pure linear. That is about the size of the ADC quantization (0.8 mV of node per count), so n is poorly constrained. Node voltage at 10 uA is 1.28-1.34 V. That is too high for one Si junction (~0.6 V) unless it is two junctions or an offset path, which is inference. In TI SLVS543S Fig 8-2, REF drives an NPN base whose emitter feeds the 3.28 kOhm / bandgap network to ANODE, a 2-Vbe-plus-resistor path. A degraded-beta TL431 input stage would look like this curve, but that is an unverified hypothesis.

hypotheses.name: Resistive leak (fixed ratio ~0.85 at all voltages; ~45-52 kOhm to GND)
hypotheses.predictions: Constant ratio. Small-signal gain 0.85. Collapse ratio 0.85. Reading in TP dips = 0.836 x V_bus.
hypotheses.evidence: TP dips: the ratio goes from 0.836-0.850 at 15.9 V to 0.929-0.946 at 12.4 V in all four events (a resistor through 0 fits with rms 5.5 uA). The J collapse needs ratio >= 0.928 even at the V-MOT = V_bus bound. investigators.summary: The fine structure of the data rules out a resistive leak. Over 0.05-16 Hz, and quasi-statically, V_rgn moves only 0.45-0.62 x as much as V_bus, with zero phase and flat gain below about 8 Hz. The static ratio is 0.835-0.852. A fixed resistor to GND would give an incremental gain equal to the static ratio. A constant-current leak or an ADC offset would give 1.0, and so would reverse-junction leakage, which is roughly voltage-independent. What fits is a superlinear, knee-type sink on the RGN-V net. It draws close to nothing below a node voltage of about 1.0 V, has a soft knee near 1.1-1.25 V, and above that has an incremental conductance of about 75-115 uS (about 9-13 kOhm), reaching 27-33 uA at 1.50-1.53 V. Three independent pieces of evidence give this curve: (a) small-signal transfer functions across 100+ bench logs and the Pi bags; (b) the ML0227 load ramp; (c) the rising leg of the TP0115 bus collapse, where the RT1987 conducts forward and V-MOT tracks V_bus. The leak's warm-up is load-independent: an exponential with tau = 5.4 +/- 0.4 min and amplitude 1.04 +/- 0.04 uA (3.3 %), with residuals uncorrelated with load. That is far too small for reverse leakage (about x2 per 10 C) and far too large for resistor TCR or ADC drift. It matches a forward/threshold junction shifting by about 10 mV during warm-up (about -2 to -4 mV/C over 3-5 C). Ground shift is at most about 1-2 mV/A at the node, so it cannot produce the static error at 0.01-0.03 A idle. If the sink is on the TL431 REF node (case A) and the linear-above-knee curve can be extrapolated, the effective chopper trip is about 30-33 V and the true V-MOT regen peaks were about 24-26 V, not 21.5 V. That extrapolation goes well beyond the measured 1.29-1.53 V node range and needs bench confirmation.

investigators.summary: The PCB design and manufacturing files show no layout or assembly-data error at the RGN-V node. The Eagle board file (references/Scale Car Board PCB 20260625.brd), the 2026-06-09 Gerbers and the PnP file all agree with each other and with the schematic. U-SNT uses TI's DBZ footprint with pad 1 to R-G (net N$36), pad 2 to RGN-V and pad 3 to GND, which matches TI's TL431 DBZ pinout (cathode 1, REF 2, anode 3). R1-SNT is 78.7k (0402) and R2-SNT is 10k (0603). On top copper, RGN-V is one island: the R1/R2 tap, U-SNT pad 2, a single 0.254 mm trace with no vias, Teensy pin 39 and the J2 probe-header pins 35/36. Its only copper neighbours are the GND pour (about 0.14-0.15 mm gap) and R1-SNT's own V-MOT pad (0.48 mm, the 0402 pad gap). No high-voltage net runs near it. CHG-V to pin 38 has the same kind of GND-pour exposure, or more, and reads correctly, so the routing itself does not explain why only RGN-V is wrong. Nothing in the repo records who assembled the board; the design BOM sources every part from DigiKey, including TI TL431BIDBZR. A generic SOT-23 TL431 with the common REF-cathode-anode order (pin 1 = REF) fitted by mistake is still possible. However, the logged data argue against it: the node follows V-MOT proportionally rather than being clamped, and the dump does not conduct. The one assembly-level mechanism specific to this node that the files leave open is contamination or flux residue under the SOT-23 or around R2-SNT, which CHG-V (resistors only) does not have. It is speculative and could only be checked on the bench.

hypotheses.name: Footprint, PnP or netlist error at U-SNT (design data maps REF to the wrong pad)
hypotheses.predictions: If REF were on pad 1 or 3 in the design data, the netlist or Gerber pads would show RGN-V reaching a pad other than 2.
hypotheses.evidence: In the brd netlist, signal RGN-V = U$1 pin '39-A15/CS/OUT1A', J2 pins 35 and 36, R1-SNT pin 1, R2-SNT pin 2, U-SNT pad 2. N$36 = U-SNT pad 1 and R-G pin 2. GND includes U-SNT pad 3. In the schematic file (Scale_Car_Board_20260624.sch), device TL431BIDBZR / DBZ0003A_N connects ANODE to 3, CATHODE to 1 and REF to 2, and net RGN-V lists U-SNT REF. TI SLVS543S Table 5-1 (p.4) gives TL431 DBZ as cathode 1, REF 2, anode 3; the TL432 is REF 1, cathode 2. In the footprint, pads 1/2/3 sit at local (-0.95,0.95), (-0.95,-0.95), (0.95,0), each 0.6x1.5 mm. With U-SNT at (115.316, 21.59) rotated R270, the absolute pads are pad 1 (116.266, 22.54), pad 2 (114.366, 22.54), pad 3 (115.316, 20.64). Those match the copper, soldermask and paste flashes in the Gerbers exactly. The RGN-V trace starts at pad 2 (114.366, 22.54) and the N$36 trace at pad 1 (116.266, 22.54). The PnP line is U-SNT 115.32 21.59 270.00 TL431BIDBZRDBZ0003A_N DBZ0003A_N.

hypotheses.name: Assembler substituted a generic SOT-23 TL431 with pin 1 = REF, pin 2 = cathode
hypotheses.predictions: Device REF would land on N$36, fed from VG (about V-MOT) through 220 ohm, and the device cathode would land on the RGN-V tap. Two outcomes are possible. (a) If REF draws mA, VG falls, the BSP170P turns on (VGS(th) -2.1/-3/-4 V) and the 47 ohm dump draws about 0.34 A continuously. (b) If REF draws little, the overdriven shunt pulls the tap down to its saturation voltage, which would barely move with V-MOT.
hypotheses.evidence: Generic parts with this pinout do exist. A GK Goodwork SOT-23 TL431 datasheet and LCSC C111578 (Shikues) are both 1 = REF, 2 = cathode, 3 = anode; LCSC C962727 (TL431N) matches TI. Nothing in the repo shows an assembler with its own parts library was used: the design BOM lists DigiKey 296-18872-1-ND (TI TL431BIDBZR), the Fusion BOM.txt carries Mouser numbers, and a grep for JLCPCB, PCBWay, LCSC, MacroFab, Seeed, turnkey, stencil and hand-solder found nothing. Against (a): the established idle bus load is 0.008-0.03 A. Against (b): the established data show the node following V-MOT. The ratio stays at 0.848 across 15.79-15.96 V, regen bursts push the node to 2.04-2.06 V with rounded peaks, and with the bus at 0 the node decays smoothly from 1.35 V to 0.2 V with tau 105-122 s. A saturated-shunt clamp would not track like that.

hypotheses.name: PCB leakage from a neighbouring high-voltage net, or an unintended short in the routing
hypotheses.predictions: A conductor near V-MOT, VG or the bus would push the node UP, not down, and a short would show as a copper connection.
hypotheses.evidence: Rasterized Gerbers (50-100 px/mm, connected-component labelling) show top-copper RGN-V as one island holding the R2 tap pad, U-SNT pad 2, the trace, Teensy pin 39 and J2 pins 35/36. Its only neighbours are the GND pour (minimum gap 0.141-0.148 mm) and R1-SNT's V-MOT pad at 0.48 mm, which is the gap between that resistor's own pads. On the bottom layer, RGN-V exists only as the through-hole barrels of Teensy 39 and J2 35/36, each in a GND-pour clearance of about 0.148 mm. In the brd, RGN-V has 13 wires, all on layer 1 and none on bottom, and 0 vias. The route runs from R1-SNT pad 1 (112.27, 17.27) down to R2-SNT, then to U-SNT pad 2, then up x = 114.366 from y 22.54 to 45.9, then to (112.27, 48.006), then along a 1.27 mm strap to Teensy pin 39 at (104.902, 48.006) and J2 at x = 107.442 and 109.982. The nearest via is a GND stitch via at (113.03, 22.606), 0.58 mm edge-to-edge from the trace. The V-MOT pour (bbox x 94.3-123.6, y 2.1-18.4) touches only R1-SNT's V-MOT pad. Copper on GND would pull the node down, but only through contamination.

hypotheses.name: Surface or ionic leak to GND that is specific to this node (flux residue under the SOT-23 between REF pad 2 and GND pad 3, or around R2-SNT)
hypotheses.predictions: Needs about 50 kohm from the tap to GND, about 31 uA at 1.52 V, rising with temperature and humidity as ionic residues do. It would show on RGN-V but not on CHG-V, because CHG-V has no SOT-23. It would clear after an IPA/flux-remover clean.
hypotheses.evidence: Geometry (computed from the brd pads): the REF pad 2 copper (x 114.066-114.666, y 21.79-23.29) is about 0.35 mm by 0.40 mm (about 0.53 mm diagonal) from GND pad 3 (x 115.016-115.616, y 19.89-21.39), all under the package body. The REF-to-cathode pad gap is 1.3 mm, but a leak from the cathode would pull the node UP, because the cathode/VG side sits near V-MOT when the dump is off. On exposure along GND (edge length within 0.25 mm of other copper; a pixel-count estimate), RGN-V has about 82 mm top plus 11 mm bottom and CHG-V about 63 mm top plus 73 mm bottom. Since CHG-V reads 0.994 x V_bus, ordinary masked-trace exposure cannot be the cause, and only the component pads differ: CHG-V has resistors only. Assembly method and cleaning are not recorded anywhere in the repo. This fits the warm-up drift in the established findings, but so does a junction leak in the TL431 or the Teensy pad, so it is not distinctive.

new_facts: The Eagle .brd 'Scale Car Board PCB 20260625.brd' is in the repo (references/) and gives the exact netlist. RGN-V = U$1 pin 39 + J2 pins 35, 36 + R1-SNT pin 1 + R2-SNT pin 2 + U-SNT pad 2. N$36 = U-SNT pad 1 + R-G pin 2. VG = R-G pin 1, R-GS pin 1, Z-SNT pin 2, Q-SNT pin 1. U-SNT pad 3 is on GND.

The schematic file Scale_Car_Board_20260624.sch maps the TL431BIDBZR device (DBZ0003A_N/M/L) as ANODE 3, CATHODE 1, REF 2. That matches TI SLVS543S Table 5-1 (p.4) for the TL431 DBZ (cathode 1, REF 2, anode 3).

The Gerbers (gerber_job.gbrjob CreationDate 2026-06-09T23:01:26Z, Fusion Electronics 9.7.0, owner Ricardo Tan) predate the brd file name (20260625) and the schematic (20260622). PnP 'PnP_Scale Car Board_front.txt': U-SNT 115.32 21.59 rot 270 DBZ0003A_N; R1-SNT 112.78 17.27 rot 0 78.7kOhm RESC1005X40; R2-SNT 112.27 19.81 rot 270 10kOhm RESC1608X60; R1-CHG 73.91 5.84 78.7kOhm 0402; R2-CHG 71.37 5.84 10kOhm 0603. Both dividers use identical value and package pairs.

investigators.summary: Nothing in the repo records anyone measuring the RGN-V node or V-MOT with a DMM at the same time as a V_rgn reading. The calibration was asked for on 2026-07-08 and again on 2026-07-28 and never done. There is also no record of the dump resistor heating, of any rework near the chopper or pin 39, or of the board's Teensy being swapped. MOT_HOTPLUG_MARGIN 3.0 V was chosen on 2026-07-08, five weeks before the first logged V_rgn, so it was never based on a measured gap. The "13.3 -> 18.1 V" note (2026-08-17b) took the 13.3 V idle reading at face value (it is 0.836 x 15.93 V); the word "held" was added later and the logs do not support it (ML0157 sits above 18.0 V for 7 ms). The main new finding comes from re-reading 8 slow bus-dip events in the bench logs (2026-08-12 to 08-25), where V-MOT follows V_bus down and back up. They show that the current drawn off the node is not a resistor and not a constant current. It is a threshold load: zero below a node voltage of about 1.19 V, then rising with about 9.5-10 kOhm slope. The fit is good (residual 1.2-3 uA, against 5-8.5 uA for a resistor to GND), and the shape is the same in every event. Two junction drops plus about 10 kOhm is the path TI's own TL431 detailed schematic (Fig 8-2) shows from REF to ANODE. A healthy part divides that current by beta (about 100); this board draws about 30 uA at 1.5 V. That points to a TL431 whose input transistor gain has collapsed (inferred), rather than the Teensy pad or a resistor. If that is right, the chopper's real trip is about 32-33 V on V-MOT (not 22.1 V), and the regen peaks already logged were really about 25 V.

hypotheses.name: U-SNT (TL431) REF input damaged or out of spec: input-transistor gain collapsed, so REF loads the node like two junction drops plus the internal emitter resistors
hypotheses.predictions: No extra load below a node voltage of about 1.19 V (V-MOT about 10.4 V); above that, load = (Vn - V0)/Rs with V0 about 1.19 V and Rs about 9.5-10 k (the healthy part has the same shape, about 100x smaller). V0 should fall about 4 mV per degC (two junctions), so the ratio falls as the board warms. Predicted readings: V-MOT 12 V reads 11.3-11.4 V; 14 V reads 12.35-12.46 V; 15.9 V reads 13.33-13.47 V; 20 V reads 15.5-15.6 V. Effective chopper trip about 32.2-32.8 V. With the Teensy pulled from its socket, the node still reads about 1.50 V at 15.9 V. A lifted TL431 measured REF-to-ANODE shows the knee.
hypotheses.evidence: Measured (inferred from logs): 8 dip events, slow and ramp-shaped with no deep collapse, all fitted to the same law: Rs 8.5-10.0 k, V0 1.168-1.235 V, knee-model residual 1.15-2.98 uA against a resistor-to-GND fit of 5.05-8.52 uA. Events: TP0115 t=1119.5 s, TP0178 804.3 s, TP0201 362.3 s, TP0209 346.4 s, WP0096/97/98/101 (script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-DC-Balancer-Board-Teensy/2dd4079b-96a3-52c6-9594-2aa3f1f11188/scratchpad/wf/repo-archaeology/dip_fit.py). Falling and rising edges agree to within about 1-2 uA; the small offset between them has the sign expected from V_bus being sampled before V_rgn (.ino:7031-7033). That rules out V-MOT lagging V_bus as the cause. Topology: TI SLVS543S Fig 8-2 (p.21) shows REF driving an NPN base, then an emitter network of 3.28k + 2.4k/7.2k into a diode-connected bandgap transistor and on to ANODE. That is two junction drops plus kOhms, and section 8.3 says REF 'is driven into an npn'. Healthy Iref is 2 typ / 4 max uA at Vref with IKA 10 mA (SLVS543S Elec Char, tl431.txt:275), about 30 uA here at only 1.5 V. A slower V0 at the later, shorter-uptime events (TP0201/TP0209 1.21-1.24 V against 1.18 V at 800-1100 s uptime) fits a negative temperature coefficient. Against: a destroyed-gain mechanism is inferred, not measured; nothing in the record says how the part could have been overstressed (no REF overcurrent path found; HBM rating ±2000 V, tl431.txt:217; handling ESD is possible).

hypotheses.name: Teensy pin-39 pad leak (ESD-structure damage), loading the same net
hypotheses.predictions: Node reads about 1.80 V at 15.9 V once the Teensy is unplugged. Swapping in another Teensy 4.1 removes the 0.85 ratio. The I-V shape would be whatever a damaged CMOS pad gives; there is no natural knee at two junction drops plus about 10 k.
hypotheses.evidence: Pin 38 sits on an identical divider and the same pad group (Eagle labels 38-A14/CS/IN1 and 39-A15/CS/OUT1A, references/Scale_Car_Board_20260624.sch net CHG-V/RGN-V) and reads 0.994 x V_bus. A healthy i.MX pad's ESD diodes do not conduct at +1.2 V to GND, and a keeper/pull-down would act like a linear resistor, which the data reject. One asymmetry favours pad stress: pin 39 has been back-biased to about 1.5 V whenever V-MOT was energised with the Teensy browned out (e.g. 2026-07-08 Death-5 round, 'Teensy browned out / USB disconnected', docs/boost-bringup-debug.md:190; WP0072/73/96/98 brownouts), while pin 38's node sat at 0 V until September. That injection is about 100 uA at most, so damage is unlikely (i.MX injection limit not in repo, TODO(verify)). The firmware never touches pin 39 except analogRead (.ino:7033): no pinMode, no SPI1, no attachInterrupt (only ENC_A/ENC_B, .ino:6736-6737), no IOMUXC writes. Every archived sketch also used 39 only as an analog input (firmware_archive/pre_board*/...ino:27/47).

hypotheses.name: Wrong or contaminated divider resistor (R1-SNT high or R2-SNT parallel leak, linear)
hypotheses.predictions: A constant ratio at every V-MOT.
hypotheses.evidence: The ratio moves from 0.837 at 15.9 V to 0.94 at 12.2 V and about 1.0 at 6-8 V within single dips (TP0115/TP0178/TP0201; WP0097 6.12/6.08). A resistor-to-GND fit leaves 5-8.5 uA residual against 1.2-3 uA for the knee model. BOM, Eagle .sch part, .brd element and PnP all give R1-SNT 78.7k / R2-SNT 10k (BOM csv lines 36-37; PnP lines 82/87; .sch:5979-5980; .brd:4111-4127).

hypotheses.name: Case B: node correct, error between node and ADC result (channel or ADC gain/offset, or a series contact resistance at the J2 socket feeding a pad leak)
hypotheses.predictions: DMM at R2-SNT reads about 1.80 V while firmware reads 1.52 V.
hypotheses.evidence: A pure ADC gain or offset error is ruled out by the voltage dependence (the offset needed would be 274 mV at 15.9 V but 84 mV at 12.2 V). Channel carry-over was already ruled out (doc section 2). The only surviving variant needs both a high-resistance J2 contact (pins 35/36 carry RGN-V, .sch net RGN-V) and a junction-like pad leak behind it. No evidence for either.

hypotheses.name: True V-MOT really is about 2.4 V below V_bus (MOT_PWR switch drop)
hypotheses.predictions: Scope V-MOT below VBUS by about 2.4 V at idle.
hypotheses.evidence: Capture 12 (2026-08-11, scope): 'the yellow (VBUS) and blue (V-MOT) traces overlap nearly everywhere' at a 15.9 V baseline (docs/boost-bringup-debug.md:1319-1331). Captures 13/14 (2026-08-12): motor node starts at 15.9 V (docs/share_sweep_whitepaper/main.tex:1115-1117). The idle load (8-30 mA) cannot drop 2.4 V across an RT1987.

hypotheses.name: 18.1 V is the chopper clamp (chopper has conducted)
hypotheses.predictions: A flat top at one fixed reading level; a slope break when the 47 ohm starts conducting.
hypotheses.evidence: Origin: the 2026-08-17b addendum read ML0151/ML0157 peaks as the clamp (docs/claude-md-archive.md:1076-1079). 'Held' appears only in later copies (HIL_PLANT.md:258, PSCAD_SIM_DESIGN.md:141/1241, '2026-08-27 bench-calibrated', archive:1367). Measured in ML0157: 66 samples above 17.5 V, 7 above 18.0 V, back to 13.3 V within about 0.3 s while I_cmd stays at -12 A. ML0151: 117 / 19 samples. No log, doc or operator note records the dump heating or conducting. Under the knee model the logged peaks (node 2.04-2.06 V) are 0.44 V short of the 2.495 V REF threshold.

investigators.summary: The logs already contain a test that sorts the candidate mechanisms, and earlier analysis missed it. The test is the incremental gain dV_rgn/dV_bus, computed from 0.2-0.5 s block means. That gain is 0.50-0.65 in 13 sessions from 2026-08-12 to 11-04 (median 0.565, correlation 0.99-1.00), against a static ratio of 0.834-0.848. A gain or reference error predicts gain = ratio, and an offset or constant-current leak predicts gain = 1.0. Only a leak whose conductance rises with node voltage gives a gain below the ratio. So any linear mechanism is refuted as the main cause: a wrong or damaged resistor, ohmic contamination, ADC gain, Vref, settling, the internal pull-down, a ground offset, or a firmware or packing error. The pad keeper is refuted as well, by its curvature and by pin 38. At a node voltage of 1.52 V the leak is about 31 uA, with an incremental conductance of about 69 uS (about 3.4 times its average conductance). From the ML0227 brackets it is no more than about 13 uA at 0.98 V. That fits a soft onset near 1.0-1.1 V followed by roughly 14.5 kOhm: about two base-emitter drops plus series resistance. The datasheet internal schematic matches this closely if the TL431 has to supply its own internal bias through REF. That happens when the cathode is open: U-SNT pin 1 unsoldered, or R-G (a 0402) open or tombstoned. A TL431 with a destroyed input stage behaves the same way. A leaking Teensy pin-39 pad and electrochemical flux leakage (the SNT cluster sits 5-8 mm from the hand-soldered J-M terminal) remain possible. A TL432 or swapped-pinout part stays refuted, but for a different reason than the doc gives. The decisive bench measurements are cheap DMM checks: node voltage, U-SNT pin 1 to VG continuity, R-G, and freeze spray.

hypotheses.name: TL431 cathode open (U-SNT pin 1 unsoldered or cracked, or R-G 220 ohm 0402 open or tombstoned), so the part powers itself through REF
hypotheses.predictions: With the cathode floating, the REF-input NPN's B-C junction (collector tied directly to CATHODE in TL431_TI.pdf Fig 8-2, p.21) forward-biases. REF current then equals the full emitter or bias current of the internal network (3.28k, 2.4k/7.2k, 800 ohm to anode) instead of I_E/beta. Prediction: about 0 below a node voltage of roughly 2 Vbe (~1.0-1.1 V), then roughly (V-1.07 V)/(5-15 kOhm). That gives tens of uA at 1.5 V and more when warm (Vbe tempco). The chopper can never trip (no gate drive), and there is no dump current, consistent with the idle bus load. Present from assembly. Pin 38 has no such part. On the bench: U-SNT pin 1 is at about REF-0.6 V (~0.9 V) on the device side while the VG pad sits at V-MOT, or R-G measures open.
hypotheses.evidence: Fits every measured feature. (1) Incremental gain 0.50-0.65 against a ratio of 0.835-0.848 (scratch a6.py: ML0135 0.621, WP0095/0100 0.565, ML0203 0.519, ML0226 0.651, ML0227 0.623; 13 sessions with corr>0.9, median 0.565). This gives a local leak conductance of ~69 uS at 31 uA: an equivalent '(V-1.07)/14.5k'. (2) ML0227 V_chg/V_bus bracket (scratch a4.py/a5.py): upper bounds on the leak are 30.9 uA at 1.52 V, 28.9 at 1.49, 17.8 at 1.33, 12.9 at 0.98 and 2.3 at 0.77 V. A 50 kOhm resistor would give 30.9/30.3/27.0/19.9/15.6. The low-voltage points are single transient samples, and the 15.2-15.5 V bins carry a possible ground-offset caveat. (3) A healthy TL431 that is off, with its cathode at about 15.9 V, draws only I_E/beta. The datasheet gives Iref 2 typ / 4 max uA at IKA 10 mA (tl431.txt line 275) and deviation 0.4-1.2 uA over temperature (line 277). So a healthy part predicts a ratio of 0.98-0.996, not 0.85. Reaching 31 uA needs effective beta near 1, which is exactly what a floating collector produces. (4) The chopper has never been shown to trip (doc section 5). No log shows the 22.13 V reading a working TL431 would produce. Not proven: no image or measurement of the solder joint, and the order-of-magnitude internal-current estimate is mine, inferred from Fig 8-2 resistor values, not from a datasheet curve.

hypotheses.name: TL431 die damaged (input-stage beta collapse or a REF-to-anode junction leak from EOS) with the cathode connected
hypotheses.predictions: Same nonlinear leak shape as the open-cathode case, an onset of about 1 V and tens of uA. The chopper may or may not still trip, at a raised level. Pin 1 measures V-MOT and R-G is intact. A swapped U-SNT clears the fault.
hypotheses.evidence: Explains the slope and the temperature drift equally well. Needs an EOS event before 2026-08-12, because the ratio was 0.8365 in the first V_rgn log (TP0074, scan.csv). A REF excursion below -0.05 mA (abs max, tl431.txt line 203) during a V-MOT negative transient is one route, unverified. It cannot be separated from the open-cathode case without probing pin 1.

hypotheses.name: Teensy pin-39 pad leak (damaged ESD or snapback clamp to VSS)
hypotheses.predictions: A nonlinear, temperature-dependent leak, larger on a hot MCU die. Lifting pin 39, or measuring the node with the Teensy unplugged (it is socketed in the J1/J2 receptacles), restores 1.80 V. The ratio should follow die temperature, so changing the CPU clock alone (set_arm_clock) would move it.
hypotheses.evidence: Curvature is plausible for a damaged clamp. Against it: the node is fed through 78.7k, which limits any V-MOT surge to about 1 mA per 80 V. That makes EOS through the divider unlikely, leaving handling ESD. No Teensy swap is recorded in the docs (grep found none). Within sessions the ratio sits flat or creeps 1-2 counts per log (scratch a10.py). Two Teensy reboots did not reset it: WP0096 at 27.9 min reads 0.8348, and WP0097-0099 at 0.1-0.5 min after a reboot also read 0.8348 (scan.csv). This weakly suggests a slow board-level thermal state rather than MCU uptime, but a soft reset need not cool the die.

hypotheses.name: Electrochemical or ionic flux-residue leakage around the RGN-V node (SNT cluster near hand-soldered THT parts)
hypotheses.predictions: Faradaic leakage with an onset near the water-splitting potential (~1.2 V), rising with temperature and humidity. That fits a ratio that falls with warm-up and shifts over weeks (0.835 in August, 0.85 from late August). The node recovers after IPA cleaning and drying.
hypotheses.evidence: From the PnP file: R1-SNT (112.78, 17.27), R2-SNT (112.27, 19.81) and U-SNT (115.32, 21.59) sit 4-8 mm from the J-M THT terminal holes (drill file: 1.6 mm holes at x 119.126, y 5.842 and 13.462; J-M placed at 119.13, 9.65). J-M is likely hand-soldered with extra flux and carries VESC current. R1-CHG/R2-CHG sit at (73.9, 5.8) and (71.4, 5.8), well away from it. 31 uA at 1.5 V would need heavy, wet residue, which makes this less likely. Shape and humidity link are not verified.

hypotheses.name: Wrong or misplaced resistor value (R2-SNT from the shared 10k reel, or R1-SNT/R1-CHG from the shared 78.7k 0402 reel), or a cracked or drifted resistor
hypotheses.predictions: A purely linear error: incremental gain equal to the ratio (0.848), flat within and between sessions (0.1% thin film; ERA-3AEB and RT0402BRD are 25 ppm/K parts per the BOM). For example, R2 = 8.2k would give a fixed 0.8370, and R1 = 95.3k a fixed 0.8424.
hypotheses.evidence: Measured incremental gain 0.42-0.65 is not 0.848, and the 'resistor plus ground offset' fit is 2.4-7x worse than the free fit on ML0203, WP0100, WP0122 and TP0132 (scratch a8.py/a9.py). Ratios above 0.8424 in late August cannot come from R1 = 95.3k. The assembly BOM (BOM.txt line 7) shows R2-SNT on an 11-part 10k line that also includes ROP1-BT/FC and RSCL/RSDA. The design CSV gives ROP1 = 40.2k, so the assembly BOM differs from the CSV (RD1 is also 243k in BOM.txt against 237k in the CSV). A reel mix-up is not impossible, but it cannot be the main mechanism. It could add a small linear part on top of the nonlinear leak.

hypotheses.name: Ohmic surface or PCB leakage to GND (about 50 kOhm)
hypotheses.predictions: Constant ratio, incremental gain 0.848.
hypotheses.evidence: Incremental gain 0.50-0.65 (scratch a6.py). Contradicts it unless the leakage is electrochemical and nonlinear (see the flux hypothesis).

hypotheses.name: i.MX RT pad keeper latched low, or the internal 100k pull-down
hypotheses.predictions: Keeper: a weak MOSFET in triode, which is sublinear (incremental conductance below average), and it would load pin 38 in the same way. Pull-down: linear, 1.52 V/100k = 15 uA, half the needed 31 uA.
hypotheses.evidence: Observed incremental conductance is about 3.4x the average (superlinear). Pin 38 is identical, starts at 0 V and is then fed (the keeper would latch it low as well), yet it reads 0.994. Firmware calls no pinMode or INPUT_DISABLE on pin 38 or 39 (grep of teensy_controller.ino), so both pads keep the same default configuration.

hypotheses.name: Ground offset between the R2-SNT/TL431 anode return and Teensy AGND
hypotheses.predictions: An additive offset of 7.87 x R_g x I in reading units, which is zero at idle. It can only lower the reading if the R2 return sits below Teensy ground.
hypotheses.evidence: The deficit is 0.85x at an idle bus load of 0.008-0.03 A. Offsets fitted to the slope data come out at -0.5 to +0.7 mOhm (free fits) and carry the wrong sign or worse residuals (scratch a8.py/a9.py). It is a possible small confound under 5-10 A loads (about 2 mOhm would add about 0.16 V reading at 10 A), which weakens only the ML0227 15.2-15.5 V bracket points.

hypotheses.name: ADC path: gain or Vref error, channel carry-over, settling with the extra node capacitance, ADC1/ADC2 module mismatch
hypotheses.predictions: All are linear in the node voltage. Vref and gain errors scale every channel together (slope = ratio). Charge-sharing carry-over depends on the previous channel.
hypotheses.evidence: Pin 38 reads 0.994 with the same scale and source impedance (teensy_controller.ino:2030 vs :2032; read order :7032-7033). The ratio is 0.84739 with V_chg at 0 V or 15.8 V (doc section 2). Incremental gain is below the ratio. Averaging of 16 is global (:6682).

hypotheses.name: Firmware scaling, macro or logging bug
hypotheses.predictions: Not applicable.
hypotheses.evidence: SCALE_V_RGN equals SCALE_V_CHG, 3.3 x 88.7/10/4095 (:2030, :2032). V_rgn is written raw into the BLG record (r.V_rgn = V_rgn, :6394; float field :5791) and the telemetry packet (:7683). Decoded values sit on integer ADC counts within 9e-5 (scratch a1.py), so there is no transformation. Pi bags agree (0.849-0.854).

hypotheses.name: Chopper loop oscillation, or aliasing of ripple
hypotheses.predictions: Oscillation needs the TL431 near Vref. Averaged ripple is linear and does not change the mean.
hypotheses.evidence: REF sits about 1 V below 2.495 V at idle, so the loop has no gain. A conducting dump would draw about 0.34 A on average, against an idle load of 0.008-0.03 A (doc section 2). ADC averaging of linear ripple keeps the mean; rectification needs a nonlinear element, which is the leak itself.

hypotheses.name: TL431 orientation error (a TL432 placed, or footprint pin mapping swapped)
hypotheses.predictions: REF would land on VG and the cathode on RGN-V. Per Fig 8-2, the REF NPN's collector is the cathode, so REF (about V-MOT through 3.3k + 220 ohm) would forward-bias B-C into the node. That injects about 4 mA, driving the node high, or turns on the Darlington, pulling VG down so the dump conducts at about 0.34 A.
hypotheses.evidence: Node reads low and the dump is off. NOTE: the doc's stated reason ('the TL431 would pull the gate down') is wrong for the pure pin-1/pin-2 swap, because the cathode would sit on the node, not VG. The conclusion still holds through the REF B-C path. Pinout confirmed: TL431 DBZ pin 1 cathode, pin 2 REF, pin 3 anode; TL432 DBZ pin 1 REF, pin 2 cathode (tl431.txt lines 166-185, Table 5-1). The anode-on-node permutations would clamp the node through the anode-to-cathode diode or turn the dump on.

hypotheses.name: Wrong part with a 1.24 V reference (TLV431-class)
hypotheses.predictions: Regulates the node at 1.24 V, so the dump would pull V-MOT down to about 11 V.
hypotheses.evidence: V-MOT tracks V_bus, and there is no standing load.

hypotheses.name: BSP170P gate, zener or R-GS path loading the node
hypotheses.predictions: These parts sit on the VG net, not RGN-V. They can affect the node only through the TL431.
hypotheses.evidence: BSP170P IGSS is 100 nA max, and VGS(th) is -2.1 to -4 V at 250 uA (BSP170P_Infineon.pdf, bsp.txt lines 95, 106). Also note: an idle-current resolution of about 8 mA/count only bounds dump current below about 10-20 mA, not to zero.

hypotheses.name: Other or unknown (e.g. leakage to a non-GND neighbouring net, Teensy socket contamination between pins 39 and 40)
hypotheses.predictions: A leak to the pin-40 INA253 output (near 0 V) would shift the ratio with I_fc by about +0.4% at 0.5 A.

remote_checks: CPU-clock die-temperature test (USB flash only, no PCB access). Log tempmonGetTemp() and V_rgn/V_bus while switching set_arm_clock between 150 and 816 MHz for a few minutes each. A ratio that follows die temperature points to the Teensy pad; no response points off-chip (TL431 or contamination).

In-situ incremental-impedance test. Briefly enable the i.MX internal pull-up (22k/47k/100k options) or pull-down on pin 39 and record the ADC shift. Calibrate the pull current on pin 38 with the charger unfed (node source impedance 8.87 kOhm). Expect Z39 of about 5.5 kOhm if g_leak is about 69 uS, against 8.87 kOhm if healthy. Repeating it at several pull settings maps the leak curve at about 1.0-1.8 V without lab access.

Read the VESC's own input voltage ('E' command, vesc.data.inpVoltage, teensy_controller.ino:9688) at idle and during a regen burst ('U' watch). This is an independent V-MOT measurement: at idle it should match V_bus, and in a burst it gives the true peak to compare with the 18.2 V V_rgn reading.
Repeat the slope test on all 21 Pi bags (index 6/7, 50 Hz, block means), and on any log where the droop MDAC codes vary at roughly constant load, to further decorrelate load from V_bus.

Inspect the gerber copper and soldermask around U-SNT pin 1 and R-G for footprint or pad-geometry problems (tombstoning risk on the 0402 R-G next to the SOT-223), and check whether the RGN-V trace runs next to GND or low-voltage nets along its ~45 mm route to pin 39.
Ask the operator for any board photos of the SNT/J-M area. Visible flux residue, a lifted U-SNT pin 1, or a tombstoned R-G would be decisive.
lab_checks: DMM on the RGN-V node at MOT_PWR closed, ~15.9 V, after warm-up. About 1.52 V means the node is loaded; about 1.80 V means the error is in the pin/ADC path.

DMM, powered: U-SNT pin 1 to GND, and pin 1 to the VG side of R-G. Healthy: both at about V-MOT (TL431 off). Open cathode joint: device pin about 0.9 V (REF - Vbc) while the VG pad is at V-MOT. Unpowered: R-G should read 220 ohm, and pin 1 to VG continuity should read about 220 ohm.
Pull the socketed Teensy (or lift pin 39) and re-measure the node from a current-limited supply. Recovery to 1.80 V means the pad leaks; no recovery means a board-side fault (TL431 or contamination).

Freeze spray, then a hot-air puff, applied separately to U-SNT, to the R1/R2-SNT area and to the Teensy, while watching the node (or the logged ratio). The element whose temperature moves the reading is the leak.

Node voltage at 3-4 V-MOT levels (e.g. 8, 12, 16, 20 V) from a current-limited supply with the VESC disconnected. This maps I_leak(V) and confirms the onset of about 1 V that a TL431-internal path would show.
If the above implicates the board: clean with IPA, dry and re-measure. Then reflow or replace U-SNT and R-G. Measure R1-SNT and R2-SNT out of circuit last (they are expected to be fine).
could_not_access: No web search was done (WebSearch/WebFetch were not loaded). The Teensy 4.1 pad-keeper default and the i.MX RT1062 pad leakage specifications come from my own background knowledge, not a fetched source.
The i.MX RT1062 datasheet (pad leakage and keeper strength) is not in references/Datasheets.

There is no TL431 datasheet curve for REF current below Vref or with the cathode open. The 'open-cathode REF current is tens of uA' figure is my order-of-magnitude estimate from Fig 8-2 resistor values, not a datasheet value.
No board photos of the SNT area, and no record of the U-SNT pin 1 or R-G solder joints.
VESC input-voltage readings were never logged alongside V_rgn, so the true V-MOT during regen is unknown.

ranking.mechanism: Damaged TL431 (U-SNT) REF input stage, correct orientation and cathode connected. The input NPN's current gain has collapsed (from ESD, handling or EOS before 2026-08-12), so REF carries roughly the full emitter-chain current (2 Vbe + internal 3.28k/2.4k network, TI SLVS543S Fig 8-2 p.21).
ranking.for: Measured: the leak curve is a threshold plus a resistor, I=(Vn-Von)/R, with Von 1.19-1.25 V and R 9.2-9.5 k, identical across four independent bus dips (TP0115/TP0178/TP0201/TP0209). I re-checked TP0178 rows 6480-6500 myself: 9.0 uA at node 1.286 V, 32.7 uA at 1.497 V, a slope of about 113 uA/V, and the falling and rising branches agree. Measured: the incremental gain dV_rgn/dV_bus is 0.50-0.65 in 13+ sessions. I re-checked ML0226: 0.651 against a static ratio of 0.848, corr 0.991. Only a superlinear sink gives that. The knee at about 2 Vbe with a series resistance of a few k matches the REF-to-ANODE path in Fig 8-2. The warm-up sign is right: Von falls, so the leak rises. A healthy part's Iref falls with temperature (Fig 6-2 p.15). The fault is specific to this node: pin 38 sits on an identical divider without a TL431 and reads 0.994.
ranking.against: The mechanism is inferred. No measurement isolates the TL431. Fitted R is about 1.6x the nominal 5.68k chain. No in-circuit overstress route exists: R1 limits REF current to below 0.5 mA even at 40 V, so handling ESD is required. The I-V alone cannot exclude a pad-side or electrochemical sink with a similar knee. The step drop in leak between 08-17 and 08-25 is unexplained; it would need annealing or about 14 C.

ranking.mechanism: TL431 cathode effectively open (U-SNT pin 1 joint open or cracked, or R-G 220 ohm 0402 open or tombstoned), so the part powers its internal bias through REF via the input NPN's base-collector junction.
ranking.for: It gives the same knee-plus-resistor REF I-V as the damaged-gain case, without needing a die-damage event. It explains a fault present from the first V_rgn log (TP0074, 2026-08-12, 0.8365). It explains why no 22.13 V trip has ever been seen: the chopper could never fire. The dump never conducts, which matches the 0.008-0.03 A idle load.
ranking.against: The 'tens of uA through REF with the cathode open' magnitude is an order-of-magnitude estimate from the Fig 8-2 resistor values (fresh-eyes), not a datasheet curve. There is no photo or joint inspection. From logs it cannot be told apart from the damaged-gain case; only a voltage reading on U-SNT pin 1 or VG, or an R-G continuity check, separates them.

ranking.mechanism: Damaged Teensy 4.1 pin-39 pad (GPIO_AD_B1_13, ESD/input structure leaking to VSS). A possible exposure route is back-injection from the charged V-MOT node (tau 105-122 s) while the Teensy was browned out.
ranking.for: An intact pad cannot draw 31 uA: IIN max 1 uA, keeper 105-175k, pull-down at most about 22 uA at 1.52 V (IMXRT1060CEC Rev4 Table 22). So a damaged pad would be pin-specific, as observed. An exposure route exists: the 2026-07-08 Death-5 brownout with V-MOT charged (docs/boost-bringup-debug.md:188). The logs cannot distinguish a pad sink from a TL431 sink.
ranking.against: A damaged CMOS pad has no natural 2-Vbe knee at 1.2 V followed by a constant 9.3k. The injection current is limited to about 0.15 mA by 8.87k. The warm-up is weakly tied to MCU uptime: a reboot did not reset it (WP0096 to WP0097-99 at 0.8348). The leak R stayed constant across 3 months while Von shifted.

ranking.mechanism: Electrochemical/ionic flux-residue leakage around U-SNT pad 2 to GND pad 3 (about 0.53 mm under the body) or around R2-SNT. The SNT cluster sits 4-8 mm from the hand-soldered J-M terminal.
ranking.for: Faradaic onset near about 1.2 V. Rises with temperature and humidity. Specific to this node: CHG-V has only resistors and sits far from J-M. The step-like leak drop between 08-17 and 08-25 (about -10 %) falls in a window with rework activity (the 74HC14 was fitted by 08-25) and could reflect cleaning or reheating.
ranking.against: 31 uA at 1.5 V needs heavy residue. Electrochemical leakage usually polarizes, drifts and depends on humidity, yet the slope R stayed fixed at 9.2-9.5k across sessions. The assembly method is not recorded anywhere.

ranking.mechanism: Case B variant: node correct, with a series break or high-resistance J2/pin-39 contact plus a nonlinear sink at the pad (error between node and ADC only)
ranking.for: It is the only form of case B left once pure ADC gain, offset and carry-over are excluded. It is decided by one DMM reading.
ranking.against: It needs two independent defects. A pure ADC/channel error is refuted by the voltage dependence: the offset would be 274 mV at 15.9 V but 84 mV at 12.2 V. Pin 38 is clean on the same ADC2 with the same settings.

ranking.mechanism: Other or unknown sink on RGN-V (e.g. contamination to a non-GND neighbour, the J2 35/36 header bridged)
ranking.for: Not excluded remotely. J2 pins 35/36 carry RGN-V with about 0.148 mm GND-pour clearance.
ranking.against: Any leak to a higher-voltage neighbour pushes the node up. Current coefficients against I_fc/I_batt are inconsistent in sign. No geometric neighbour other than GND.

ranking.mechanism: Linear divider fault (wrong or drifted R1-SNT/R2-SNT, ohmic contamination about 50k, ADC gain/Vref, firmware scaling)
ranking.for: A shared 10k reel (11 parts) and a shared 78.7k reel in the assembly BOM make a reel mix-up conceivable.
ranking.against: Refuted as the main cause by an incremental gain of 0.50-0.65 against a ratio of 0.835-0.85. The ratio rises to about 0.94 at 12.2 V within a single dip. SCALE_V_RGN equals SCALE_V_CHG (.ino:2030/2032). Logged values are raw ADC counts.

ranking.mechanism: Swapped/second-source TL431 pinout (pin1 REF, e.g. TL432/CJ431-style) on the TI DBZ footprint
ranking.for: The REF-K-A order is common among second sources (CJ431, GK, LCSC C111578).
ranking.against: It would predict a continuous dump at 0.34 A / 5.4 W and REF at 4-13 mA (over the 10 mA abs max). Measured idle load is 0-0.03 A, and post-peak decay bounds the V-MOT load to 7-20 mA. The design data are verified: brd/gerber/PnP map pad1=N$36 (R-G), pad2=RGN-V, pad3=GND, matching TI DBZ (SLVS543S Table 5-1). The BOM orders a genuine TI TL431BIDBZR (BOM csv line 35).

key_uncertainties: Case A vs case B has never been decided. No DMM or scope reading of the RGN-V node taken alongside a V_rgn sample exists anywhere in the repo. It was requested 2026-07-08 (docs/boost-bringup-debug.md:212) and 2026-07-28 (docs/design-review-2026-07-28.md:140) and is still open in WORK_QUEUE.md:8. Every safety extrapolation below assumes case A.

Location of the sink. Data fix its I-V shape (measured) but not its site. The TL431 input stage (two variants), the Teensy pad and flux residue all load the same net. The 2Vbe-plus-resistor shape favours the TL431 only by inference from TI Fig 8-2.
Damaged-gain TL431 vs open cathode / open R-G. Indistinguishable from logs. It matters for safety: the damaged-gain case predicts a trip near 33 V; the open-cathode case predicts no trip at all.

Behaviour above node 1.536 V is extrapolated. The '33 V effective trip' and the '~25 V true regen peaks' assume the leak stays linear above the measured 1.29-1.53 V node range. No regen burst was ever logged with an independent V-MOT reference (REGEN closed, or VESC inpVoltage).
Below node ~1.0 V the evidence is single 1 kHz transient samples with +/-3-7 uA timing error (WP0097, ML0227 collapse). 'Leak ~0 below the knee' is medium confidence.

Cause of the 08-17 to 08-25 step (leak about -10 %, Von +50-60 mV, R unchanged). No rework or cleaning record exists for that window. If a joint was reflowed or the board cleaned then, that would favour the open-joint or flux hypotheses.
Whether the board Teensy was ever swapped, unplugged or ESD-exposed. Not recorded; telemetry carries no Teensy ID.
Who assembled the board and with what flux and cleaning. Not recorded. The U-SNT top marking is unverified (genuine TI vs substitute).
RT1987 POVP strapping on D-MT/D-BRG (23 V vs 33 V OVP option, RT1987_DS-00 p.6). This matters if true regen peaks really reached ~25 V. Not checked.
