lab_plan: 1. (2 min, DMM, powered, MOT_PWR closed, ~15.9 V, after 10-15 min warm-up) Measure the RGN-V node at R2-SNT top / U-SNT pin 2, then at the Teensy pin-39 header. Both ~1.52 V means case A (node loaded). R2 top 1.80 V with pin 39 at 1.52 V means a series break plus a pad sink. 1.80 V at both means an ADC-path fault. In the same session, measure the voltage across R-GS (VG to V-MOT): about 0 V as designed, 11-13 V would mean a swapped part. Touch-check R-SHUNT (should be at ambient).

2. (1 min, DMM, same powered state) Measure U-SNT pin 1 on the device lead itself, and the VG side of R-G, both to GND. Both ~V-MOT: cathode connected. Device pin ~0.9 V with the VG pad at V-MOT: open cathode joint or open R-G. Unpowered, R-G should read ~220 ohm from U-SNT pin 1 to VG. This splits the two TL431 variants and costs nothing.

3. (5 min, no solder) Unplug the Teensy from the J1/J2 receptacles. Feed V-MOT from a current-limited bench supply with the VESC disconnected, MOT_PWR not required. DMM the node. Recovery to V-MOT/8.87 means the pad is the sink. Still loaded means a board-side sink. Alternatively, swap in the spare HIL Teensy 4.1 and log the ratio.

4. (10 min, Teensy out, current-limited supply, keep V-MOT <= 20 V) Sweep V-MOT at 8/10/12/14/16/18 V and DMM the node. Threshold model: 0.902/1.127 (ideal) then ~1.28-1.30 at 12 V, 1.39-1.42 at 14 V, 1.50-1.53 at 16 V, ~1.63 at 18 V. A constant ratio would instead indicate a linear fault.

5. (5 min) Freeze-spray or warm with low-flow hot air, separately, U-SNT, the R1/R2-SNT area and (if fitted) the Teensy, while watching the node. The element whose temperature moves the reading (cooling raises the node about 2 mV/C at the node under the TL431 model) is the sink.

6. (15 min) If board-side: clean the U-SNT/R2-SNT area with IPA or flux remover, dry, and re-measure. Recovery means residue. If no recovery: lift U-SNT pin 2, or replace U-SNT with a new TL431BIDBZR and reflow/check R-G. Re-measure (expect 1.796 V at 15.93 V). Curve-trace the removed part REF-to-ANODE with the cathode at ~15 V through ~3.5k. Damaged-part prediction is ~30 uA at 1.5 V with a ~1.2 V knee; a new part draws under 1 uA.

7. (last, only after the sink is removed) Run the chopper trip test: slow, current-limited V-MOT ramp with the VESC disconnected, watching R-SHUNT current. Expect a trip at ~22.1 V. Do NOT ramp toward 30+ V with the original part fitted; if you must, stop at ~28 V and expect no trip.
safety_implications: If case A holds (node genuinely loaded, which is the most likely outcome; ~0.93 combined probability over the node-side mechanisms), the TL431/BSP170P chopper does NOT clamp at 22.13 V. With a damaged-gain TL431 the extrapolated trip is ~30-33 V (inferred). With an open cathode or open R-G the chopper cannot trip at all. Either way the board has no verified fast regen clamp below the RT1987's 32 V operating rating, and the CAL 470 uF / C-D6 10 uF parts are rated 35 V (BOM csv lines 30, 81).

The logged regen peaks (18.11-18.26 V reading) are probably ~24.6-25.7 V true V-MOT, not ~21.4 V. This extrapolates beyond the measured node range. If confirmed, existing vehicle runs have already approached the VESC input limit (VESC EDU firmware HW_LIM_VIN 27 V per vedderb/bldc hw_edu_core.h) and possibly an RT1987 23 V OVP option. Until the node is fixed, limit regen severity (VESC regen current / braking limits) on the vehicle.

Do NOT apply the planned fw v38 fixed correction (SCALE_V_RGN x 1/0.8505, docs/reviews/fw36_regen_2026-11-04/README.md:153). The error is nonlinear: a fixed factor reads correctly only near 15.9 V and under-reads V-MOT increasingly above it, and over-reads below ~14 V. FAULT_OV_RGN (28 V reading, .ino:2284) is effectively unreachable, and any V_rgn-based regen/OV logic is unreliable until the hardware is fixed.

MOT_HOTPLUG_MARGIN (3.0 V, .ino:2347) was never calibrated against a measured V_rgn gap, and the V_rgn deficit at 15.9 V is ~2.4-2.6 V. The hot-plug guard therefore operates on a reading that is ~2.5 V low at full bus. Review its margin logic before relying on it for bring-up.
Bench trip testing with the original U-SNT fitted must keep V-MOT well below 32 V. Replace and verify the part before any trip test.

Lab probing should use a current-limited supply with the VESC disconnected. Do not short pin 2 to pin 1 of the SOT-23 with a probe: this would pull VG down and turn on the 47 ohm dump at ~0.34 A / 5.4 W.
synthesis.report:
SYNTHESIS: the V_rgn ~0.85 x V_bus mismatch (Teensy pin 39, RGN-V net)

1. What is now established, and how firmly

MEASURED. The error is a real nonlinear current sink, not a linear scale error. Two independent signatures show it.
(a) Incremental gain. dV_rgn/dV_bus from 0.2-0.5 s block means is 0.50-0.65 in 13+ sessions, against a static ratio of 0.834-0.852 (fresh-eyes a6.py; data-thermal-noise tf.py/inc2.py; data-leak-curve). I re-checked ML0226 (logs/ML0226/ML0226.csv): slope 0.651, corr 0.991, static ratio 0.848. The predictions are: a resistor or gain fault gives gain = ratio (0.85); an offset or constant current gives 1.0; only a leak whose conductance rises with node voltage gives a gain below the ratio. The obvious confound, RT1987 Ron x load, moves the gain the other way (above the ratio), so it cannot produce this.
(b) Bus-dip I-V. In four motor-load bus dips (TP0115 08-13, TP0178 08-17, TP0201 and TP0209 08-25), V-MOT follows V_bus through the forward-conducting RT1987: V_rgn rises on the same sample as V_bus. They give the same law, I_leak = (Vn - Von)/R, with Von 1.19-1.25 V and R 9.2-9.5 k, rms ~1 uA. A resistor fits with rms 5.5-7 uA and a constant current with ~8 uA. I re-checked TP0178 rows 6480-6500 myself: 32.7 uA at node 1.497 V falling to 9.0 uA at 1.286 V (ratio 0.836 -> 0.939), a slope of ~113 uA/V, with the falling and rising branches agreeing. R is constant across sessions; Von moves with the session baseline (1.19 V at ratio 0.836, 1.23-1.25 V at 0.845-0.850). ML0227's V_chg/V_bus bracket at node 1.485 V (23.2-28.4 uA) matches the model's 25.5 uA. The low-voltage collapse samples put the leak near 0 at node ~0.7-1.0 V (single transient samples; medium confidence).
(c) Thermal. The warm-up is a load-independent exponential: tau 5.4 +/- 0.4 min, amplitude +1.04 uA (3.3 %), over 9 boots (data-thermal-noise fitexp.py). That fits a forward-junction threshold shift of ~10 mV. It does not fit reverse leakage (far too small a change) or resistor TCR (far too large).

DATASHEET INFERENCE. A healthy TL431BI's REF current is 2 typ / 4 max uA (+2.5 uA over temperature) (TI SLVS543S Table 6.12, references/Datasheets/TL431_TI.pdf), which gives a ratio >= 0.968, and it FALLS with temperature (Fig 6-2 p.15). The observed leak is 8-15x larger with the opposite temperature sign. The TL431 REF input is the base of an NPN whose emitter runs through 3.28k and then a 2.4k/7.2k network into diode-connected/bandgap transistors to ANODE, with its collector on CATHODE (Fig 8-2 p.21). The measured shape, ~2 Vbe onset plus a few-k slope, is what that path delivers if the 1/beta division is lost.

2. Reconciled conflicts

- Swapped pinout. All eight reports reject it. The design data are verified independently: brd/gerbers/PnP give pad1 = N$36 (R-G), pad2 = RGN-V, pad3 = GND, matching TI DBZ (SLVS543S Table 5-1), and the BOM orders the genuine TI part (BOM csv line 35). On the data side, the predicted 0.34 A dump against the measured 0-0.03 A idle load, and the 7-20 mA post-peak decay bound, rule it out. Fresh-eyes notes that the existing doc's stated reason is wrong for a pure 1/2 swap (the cathode would land on the node, not VG); the conclusion still stands via the REF B-C path.
- Teensy pad: the reports assign 0.15-0.30. The teensy-pad investigator rules out every intact-pad mechanism (keeper 105-175k, pull-down <= ~22 uA at 1.52 V, IIN 1 uA, settling 87 tau; IMXRT1060CEC Rev4 Tables 22/54/55), so only a damaged pad remains. I put it at 0.19. The 2Vbe+R shape and the constant R across 3 months fit a bipolar input chain better than a damaged CMOS clamp, and a reboot did not reset the drift (WP0096 -> WP0097-99 at 0.8348). The logs still cannot exclude it, and the J1/J2 socket makes it the cheapest thing to test.
- Damaged-gain TL431 vs open cathode (fresh-eyes). Both route full internal current through REF and give the same I-V. They differ only in whether a trip still exists (~33 V vs never). I split the TL431 mass 0.36 / 0.26. The open-joint variant needs no unexplained ESD event; the damaged-die variant needs one before 2026-08-12, because R1 limits REF current to below 0.5 mA in circuit.
- The '18.1 V clamp' in the HIL/PSCAD docs. Repo-archaeology traced it to the 2026-08-17b analysis of ML0151/ML0157. The 'held' wording was added later. ML0157 has only 7 samples above 18.0 V. checks_performed: Rendered TI SLVS543S Fig 8-2 (p.21) at 250/600 dpi (scratch wf/verify-physics/fig82c.png, refzoom.png). The REF pin connects to two internal elements: (a) the base of input NPN Q1, whose collector goes to CATHODE and whose emitter runs to 3.28k, then to 2.4k plus a diode-connected NPN, in parallel with 7.2k into the bandgap transistor's collector, and on to ANODE. (b) A diode-connected PNP: emitter on the REF line, base and collector tied to the output-drive node, which is the base of the 150 ohm / 10 kohm Darlington whose collectors are on CATHODE. The synthesis covers only path (a).
Recomputed the leak at 15.93 V with the node at 1.522 V: (15.93-1.522)/78.7k - 1.522/10k = 30.87 uA. This matches the synthesis's ~31 uA.
Recomputed the TP0178 chord from the synthesis's two points (9.0 uA at 1.286 V, 32.7 uA at 1.497 V): R = 8.90 kohm, Von = 1.206 V. This is consistent with the stated 9.2-9.5k / 1.19-1.25 V.

Recomputed the incremental gain for a node sink of slope R: gain = (1/R1)/(1/R1+1/R2+1/R) x 8.87. R = 9.3k gives 0.512. The ML0226 figure of 0.651 corresponds to R = 16.5k, not 9.3k. So the quoted gain range 0.50-0.65 spans slopes of 9-16.5k and is not one constant R. Not a refutation, but the 'constant R' claim holds only for the dip I-V, not for the gain data.

Diode dynamic resistance: two junctions at 20 uA give 2Vt/I = 2.6 kohm, which adds to any chain-resistor slope. On path (a) with Q1 beta near 0, the slope is about 5.68k (less with the 7.2k branch in parallel) plus 2.6k, about 7-8.3k. Reaching 9.3k then needs (beta+1) of only about 1.1-1.3. That is near-total loss of gain, more extreme than the synthesis's '1.6x' reading suggests.

Path (b) with the Darlington's first transistor carrying no collector current (cathode open, or that transistor damaged): the REF current is Veb(PNP) + Vbe(Qa) into 150 + 10k ohm. The knee is about 2 Vbe and the slope about 10.15k plus 2.6k of dynamic resistance. At node 1.522 V and a 1.22 V knee this gives about 30 uA. This matches the measured magnitude without any beta-collapse assumption (inferred; IC resistor tolerance not published).

Linear extrapolation check: trip at REF 2.495 V gives 32.9 V V-MOT. A regen reading of 18.09/18.27 V (node 2.04/2.06 V) gives 25.0/25.4 V true. These match the synthesis's numbers but depend entirely on the leak staying linear.

Healthy-part bounds confirmed: Iref 2 typ / 4 max uA and II(dev) up to 2.5 uA (tl431.txt lines 275-277, 317-319); Ioff 0.1-1 uA (line 282); IREF >= 4 uA needed (p.22 text). Fig 6-2 is 'Reference Current vs Free-Air Temperature' (line 655).

errors_found: Incomplete device model. TI Fig 8-2 has a second REF-to-ANODE route: a diode-connected PNP from REF into the output-drive node, then the Darlington base-emitter into 150 ohm + 10 kohm. The synthesis attributes the knee-plus-resistor I-V only to Q1's emitter chain. This second path gives a ~2 Vbe knee and a ~10k slope naturally. So the 'damaged Q1 input NPN' sub-mechanism is not uniquely supported by the I-V shape.

The Q1 beta-collapse story understates what it needs. Once the two-junction dynamic resistance (~2.6k at 20 uA) and the 7.2k parallel branch are counted, matching 9.3k needs (beta+1) of about 1.1-1.3 at tens of uA. That is essentially a dead transistor, not merely a 'collapsed' gain. 'Fitted R ~1.6x nominal' is not the right reading of the mismatch.

The safety extrapolations (trip ~30-33 V, regen peaks ~25 V true) assume the leak stays linear above node 1.536 V. Under path (b), the Darlington's second transistor (Qb) base-emitter clamps the 10k once ~0.6 V sits across it, at about 60 uA. That is a node of about 1.8-1.9 V, inside the regen-peak range of 2.04-2.06 V. Above that the sink would steepen sharply into a soft clamp near 2 V at the node, about 18 V on the reading. The 18.1-18.3 V regen 'ceiling' could then be the clamp, and true V-MOT could exceed 25 V. On this model the 25 V figure is a lower bound, not an estimate.

The 'constant R 9.2-9.5k' framing conflicts with the quoted incremental-gain range. A gain of 0.651 (ML0226) implies an incremental slope of about 16.5k at node ~1.52 V, against 9.3k for a gain of 0.51. The gain data and the dip I-V do not describe a single linear-plus-knee sink without an extra effect (RT1987 Ron, filtering, or a convex I-V).

A diode-connected PNP runs from REF into the output-drive node, which then reaches ANODE through the Darlington base-emitter and 150 ohm + 10 kohm. If the first Darlington transistor carries no collector current, that route gives about 2 Vbe + 10.15k. That yields ~30 uA at node 1.52 V without assuming beta near 1 in Q1. errors_found: The incremental gain is internally inconsistent with the dip-fitted slope. Measured, from logs/ML0226/ML0226.csv with 0.3 s block means (1407 blocks): dV_rgn/dV_bus = 0.649, corr 0.991. Controlling for bus current (I_fc+I_batt) gives 0.637; controlling for current and time gives 0.607. A threshold-plus-resistor leak with R = 9.3 k predicts 8.87*G1/(G1+G2+1/9.3k) = 0.51 (inferred). 0.61-0.65 implies a local slope of about 13.7-16.6 k at node 1.52 V. That contradicts 'R 9.2-9.5k identical' if R is meant to hold through November, and a diode-like curve would push the gain the other way (local R at the top of the curve <= 9.3 k). The most likely cause is a positive bias in the load-driven incremental gain: V-MOT = V_bus - I*R through the switch, plus regen moments. So the incremental gain supports nonlinearity qualitatively, but it should not be quoted as a match to the dip slope.

All four 'independent' dip events have the same physical type: a source-less share-handoff collapse, with I_fc = I_batt = 0 for ~5 ms and the bus falling at ~0.6-0.7 V/ms. Each event gives 6 dip samples, only 12 fit points in total (TP0178 rows 6486-6495). They are independent in date but not in stimulus, and each one rests on V-MOT tracking V_bus through the RT1987 during that collapse.

Minor wording: the synthesis says that in TP0178 'falling and rising branches agree'. Measured: the rising branch runs about +0.006-0.008 in ratio above the falling branch at equal V_bus (e.g. 12.98 V rising 0.912 vs ~0.906 interpolated falling; 13.85 V 0.889 vs ~0.881). This is consistent with V_rgn being sampled slightly after V_bus in the loop at ~0.7 V/ms slew (~0.1-0.2 ms skew, inferred). It is not exact agreement. It is symmetric around the static law, so the fit stands.

The ML0215-ML0217 dark-decay tau of 105-122 s does not discriminate between any of the mechanisms. At V_rgn readings of 1.35 -> 0.2 V the node is 0.15-0.02 V, far below the knee, so every hypothesis predicts the same decay. Also, 480 uF x 88.7 k = 42.6 s is SHORTER than the observed tau. That implies additional capacitance on V-MOT (the VESC's own bulk caps, inferred ~1.2-1.4 mF total) or a feed. It is not evidence for or against any sink, and it should not be used to bound the V-MOT load without accounting for the VESC capacitance.

errors_found: The argument against the pad, 'a reboot did not reset the warm-up (WP0096 -> WP0097-99 at 0.8348)', is invalid. The warm-up is load-independent with tau 5.4 min on MCU uptime. If anything this suits the Teensy's constant self-heating at least as well as board-side heating, since at idle the board dissipates little. The synthesis counts the thermal sign for the TL431 and against the pad. It is neutral at best.

The '2 Vbe knee' is the x-intercept of a straight line fitted over node 1.29-1.53 V, a 0.24 V span. Any superlinear sink gives an intercept somewhere. For example, a diode plus series resistance reproduces the TP0178 points (9.0 uA at 1.286 V, 32.7 uA at 1.497 V: a ratio of 3.63 over 0.211 V). Below the knee there are only low-quality single collapse samples, which the synthesis itself admits. The fitted R (9.2-9.5k) is about 1.6x the TL431 internal 5.68k chain. The matrix is internally inconsistent. The 'No 22.13 V reading ever' row marks the pad 'NO' but its text says the trip would also move to about 33 V because the node is loaded. verdicts.strongest_counterargument: Every log signature fixes only the I-V shape of a sink on RGN-V, not where it sits. Measured: V-MOT is about V_bus, because V_chg reads V-MOT through REGEN at 0.994 while V_rgn reads 0.847 at the same time (ML0227). The leak is superlinear: incremental gain 0.65 against a ratio of 0.848 in ML0226, and the dip I-V. It is about 31 uA at 1.5 V and grows with uptime. A damaged Teensy pad (a socketed, handled part with direct header exposure), a TL431 with an open cathode or tombstoned 0402 R-G, a TL431 with a damaged input, and ionic residue under the SOT-23 all give a superlinear sink of tens of uA. The features the synthesis uses to favour the damaged-gain TL431 do not single it out: a 2 Vbe-looking intercept from a 0.24 V-wide linear fit, an R that is 1.6x the datasheet chain, and a thermal response and a 'reboot' that a warm die explains equally well. The damaged-gain variant also needs an unexplained ESD event, while the open-joint variant needs none. So the top entry should not be top, and the TL431-vs-pad split is roughly even on remote data. Only removing the Teensy, or probing U-SNT pin 1/VG, decides it. That is a 5-minute lab step and needs no further remote analysis.
